description.value: The study characterized shared gray- and white-matter neurostructural changes in behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis compared with healthy controls using multimodal MRI.

spans.text: In the present multimodal magnetic resonance study, we characterized the site and extent of shared neurostructural changes in gray and white matter in 20 bvFTD and 19 ALS patients without dementia.

description.value: Observational cross-sectional multimodal MRI study of bvFTD, ALS, and healthy control groups.

spans.text: The aim of the present study is to measure both commonalities and differences across bvFTD and ALS compared with healthy controls (HCs).

Whole-brain DTI images were acquired using a single-shot echo planar sequence (TR/TE = 8986/80 ms; FOV = 240 mm 2 ; 56 sections; 2.5 mm isotropic resolution) with parallel imaging (SENSE factor = 2.5) and diffusion gradients applied along 32 noncollinear directions (b-value = 1000 s/mm 2 ).

definition.value: A widespread FA reduction in bvFTD compared with HC.

spans.text: We tested the presence of WM microstructural changes in the 2 patient groups compared with controls separately—that is, ALS versus HC and bvFTD versus HC—setting a number of 10,000 random permutations per contrast.

value: We found a widespread FA reduction, mainly involving the limbic-prefrontal circuitry, and including the uncinate, inferior fronto-occipital, inferior longitudinal fasciculi, and the anterior portion of the cingulum bundle. This pattern also encompassed a consistent FA alteration along the forceps minor, the corpus callosum, the superior longitudinal fasciculus, the corticospinal tract and the fornix.

footer.value: Percent variations of WM microstructure across patient subgroups have been computed by extracting mean values from the WM conjunction cluster, including the CC body and the right CST. Negative percentages correspond to lower FA/MO values (e.g., higher microstructural reduction), and positive percentages correspond to higher FA/MO values (e.g., lower microstructural reduction) in subgroups listed on rows compared with subgroups listed on columns.
